clue.text: Far from the first dance, not the last one, and not the first part of the year

indicators.note: the final letter of the dance is dropped

parts.note: a quadrille is a square dance for four couples
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the opening letter of that part of the year is dropped

parts.note: a month is one part of the year

explanation.surface: A ballroom programme note: far from the first dance, nor the last, nor early in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the last' trims QUADRILLE to QUADRILL; 'not the first' trims MONTH to ONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrillionth item in a sequence is enormously distant from being first in line.

clue.text: Single girl struck, but not put down

parts.note: Una is a girl's name that also means one in Latin
bashed means struck

explanation.surface: A lone girl was hit but refused to be crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed is undaunted, not humbled or put down by anything.

clue.text: Deferment of French poem

parts.note: de is French for of
a lay is a narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: A French poem whose publication has been put off.
explanation.definitionFit: A delay is a postponement, the act of deferring something.

clue.text: Araucaria's favourite Guardian incentive

parts.note: the setter Araucaria speaking of himself: Araucaria is, so I'm
a pet is a favourite
the Guardian newspaper speaking of itself as we, hence us

explanation.surface: The setter's preferred motivation, as offered by his paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was this puzzle's setter and the Guardian its newspaper, so both stand for the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is a driving force or stimulus, much like an incentive.

clue.text: One that won't stand up is about right with a plate

definitions.note: describes a person, as a noun phrase would

indicators.note: the leaner surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a leaner is one who leans rather than standing upright

explanation.surface: Someone slouching, it seems, is near a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers must display L-plates, so 'with a plate' fairly describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner driver in Britain carries an L-plate on the car, so is someone with a plate.

clue.text: Be more than anaesthetised by anaesthetic?

parts.note: someone anaesthetised is out cold
an anaesthetic is a thing that numbs, a numb-er

explanation.surface: Asks whether a patient can be more knocked out by an anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'anaesthetic' as NUMB-ER, something that makes numb, not the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber is to exceed in quantity, to be more than another group.

clue.text: It's not corruption

definitions.meaning: the contraction '... is dialect for it is not
a stain of moral or physical contamination

explanation.definitionFit: Taint means contamination or corruption, and spelt 'tain't it is a contraction of it ain't.

clue.text: 13 with groove, perhaps, not living at home after marriage?

definitions.note: 13 is the answer to 13-across, a tongue; tongue and groove joins boards

indicators.note: the boarding piece follows the marriage piece

parts.note: a match is a marriage
boarding means lodging away from home, as at boarding school

explanation.surface: Asks whether a newly-wed couple who left home might be tongue-tied.
explanation.walkthrough: Matchboarding is boards joined by tongue and groove, the tongue coming from 13-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchboarding is timber cladding made of boards fitted together by tongue-and-groove joints.

clue.text: Officer's vehicle going all out?

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Asks whether a senior officer's car is being driven flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going all out' suggests effort, but here it means every worker walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: In a general strike workers across all industries go out, a pun on the idiom for full effort.

clue.text: Wallpaper showing horse at play, playing outside

indicators.note: the jumble goes round the horse
the letters of at and play are set playing, jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A wallpaper design showing a horse frolicking outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at play' reads as a description of the horse, but those two words are the fodder that 'playing' jumbles into ALYPTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaglypta is a brand of embossed wallpaper, used here as a type of wallcovering.

clue.text: Time to drink a twist

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Time for a cocktail with a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist strands together or wind around something.

clue.text: Nuts at last eaten by fish

indicators.note: the fish swallows the next piece

parts.note: cray is short for crayfish
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Nuts finally being consumed by a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' means the alphabet's final letter, not the last letter of 'Nuts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts and crazy are both informal words for mad.

clue.text: I won't let you speak, for example, to unite cast

indicators.note: the letters are cast, thrown into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone casting a spell to unite people while silencing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges EG, TO and UNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-tie could say this: the condition literally prevents free speech.

clue.text: Lamb's remarks about Bacon in the Atlantic

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for the islands located there

indicators.note: the bleats go round the next piece

parts.note: a lamb's bleats are baas
ham is cured pork like bacon

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb commenting on Francis Bacon while crossing the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the writers Charles Lamb and Francis Bacon; really they are a sheep and pork.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahamas are an island nation lying in the Atlantic Ocean east of Florida.

clue.text: Whirlpool in the West: fifty corpses resurrected

parts.note: Mae West, the American film star
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: raised up, so the word is turned upside down in a down clue

parts.note: morts, French for the dead

explanation.surface: A whirlpool out west where fifty bodies have been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the West' sounds like a direction, but means the actress Mae West; 'resurrected' raises MORTS to STROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, originally one off the Norwegian coast.

clue.text: Polish measure for a 26

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Instructions for polishing and measuring something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is the medical name for German measles, the answer at 26-across.

clue.text: Fish the only answer…

parts.note: the answer is a lemon: a lemon is a dud response that answers nothing
sole means only

explanation.surface: Declaring a fish dish the only solution, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 19 down: after soup, fish is the only course.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is an edible flatfish of European waters.

clue.text: Speak at home to publicise what one is wearing?

parts.note: an ad publicises something
a dress is what one wears

explanation.surface: Giving a talk at home to show off one's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' is a second hint, since your address is where you live.
explanation.definitionFit: To address an audience is to speak to it formally.

clue.text: … the former course with dash

parts.note: soup is served as the course before the fish
con is Italian for with, as in con brio

explanation.surface: Continuing the meal: the earlier course had a dash of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 17 down: soup comes before the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount, a dash or hint.

clue.text: Invest in lots of paper to speak of ancient craft

indicators.note: signals the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to buy reams is to purchase lots of paper

explanation.surface: A stationery shopper chatting about historic ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Republican gets a shilling benefit

parts.note: a bob was British slang for a shilling, an old coin worth 12 pence
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A Republican receives a little welfare money.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Dole was a US Republican senator and presidential candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dole was a prominent American Republican politician, the 1996 presidential nominee.

clue.text: Delete current measures and start petty complaint that will fizzle out

definitions.note: describes a thing, as the noun answer does

parts.note: D is the proof-reader's mark for delete
amps measure electric current

indicators.note: only the opening of the complaint is used

parts.note: a quibble is a petty objection

explanation.surface: A minor grievance that will soon fade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' keeps QUIB, the beginning of QUIBBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a let-down, something that fails to go off as expected.

clue.text: Short life in French film?

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time
vie is French for life

explanation.surface: Asks whether a brief French life story would make a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a film, especially in American usage.

clue.text: I give a fellow gold

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Presenting a man with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives, so could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Composer unhappy about… about country

indicators.note: the sad word goes around the country

parts.note: sad means unhappy
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A composer who is gloomy about his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue; the repeated 'about' is not decoration, as each one signals a different operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was a French composer, best known for The Sorcerer's Apprentice.

clue.text: Return most of my income? Certainly not!

indicators.note: the remaining letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: revenue is income

explanation.surface: A taxpayer refusing to file a return on income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims REVENUE to REVEN and 'Return' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Never is an emphatic no, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Regular feature of canal with stopper outside

indicators.note: the stopper is put round the other pieces

parts.note: a cork is a bottle stopper
a lock is a gated section on a canal

explanation.surface: A canal feature sealed with a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like clockwork is perfectly regular and predictable.

clue.text: Spots convergence of same river and same glen

definitions.note: a plural noun for the rash, where the answer is a singular illness

indicators.note: the pieces flow together and mix into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geographer spotting where two rivers meet in a glen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convergence of' mixes SAME, R, SAME and GLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is a disease known for its rash of red spots.
